newsitem.title: UK: British Airways makes 127 mln stg charge.
newsitem.headline: British Airways makes 127 mln stg charge.

text.p: British Airways Plc announced record profits on Monday and gave its 58,210 staff a bonus of 10 free shares each as well as 89 million pounds ($145.8 million) from the profits.

The company made an exceptional charge of 127 million pounds to cover restructuring costs associated with its "Business Efficiency" programme, but also wrote back in an exceptional gain of 125 million pounds as a result of restating at original cost its investment in USAirways, reversing the 50 percent write-down made two years ago.

The company reported a 9.4 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 640 million pounds for the year to March 31, 1997 which was achieved despite a 20 percent rise in fuel costs and a strong pound. It recommended a final dividend of 10.80 pence a share, giving a total dividend of 15.05 pence, up 10.3 percent.

Looking ahead, chairman Sir Colin Marshall said economic conditions are expected to produce continuing growth in demand for air travel, while the adverse affect of sterling's strength will be partially offset by lower fuel costs.

"Sterling's current strength will adversely impact profits although it is anticipated that this will at least partially be offset by lower fuel prices and further business efficiency improvement," Marshall said in a statement.

The share of profits to be paid to employees is equivalent to 3.3 weeks' basic pay, with a minimum of almost 1,100 pounds for those in the UK. The company said the 10 free shares to given to employees is to mark their efforts in a "particularly demanding" year and to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the company's privatisation.
